Despite this, the management personally requested me to remove my previous review and give them a chance to correct their mistake. Trusting them, I deleted it and visited again. I was told the facial would last 45 minutes, yet the entire service was rushed and completed in barely 25 minutes, with only 3–5 minutes of actual massage. When questioned, the response was simply “we will look into it,” with no accountability or resolution. To make it worse, the beautician mentioned that the offer is technically for new visitors only but they are “still giving it to everyone” — as if it is a favor. If that is the policy, it should be transparently stated in the promotion instead of being disclosed verbally later.

This reflects a clear pattern of misleading communication, rushed services, inconsistent pricing explanations, and poor customer handling. Running offers does not mean compromising honesty, professionalism, or value for money. Extremely disappointing experience — twice. Customers deserve transparency, respect, and the service quality they are promised.

It’s now been over 30 days, and not only has there been no visible improvement, but I’ve actually had to lighten my eyebrow hair myself just to make it look presentable. I’ve stopped taking pictures or have to wear big glasses to hide how it looks.

Now I’m being told it takes 45–60 days to heal and that I may need multiple sessions. This was never communicated earlier. If I had been told upfront that it would take 2–3 (or more) sessions, I would have reconsidered entirely. Repeated corrections on already overworked brows is not something I’m comfortable with.

What’s most disappointing is the lack of accountability. The artist is unwilling to acknowledge the miscommunication, and the team refused to share the owner’s contact details when I requested escalation.

I paid ₹50,000 for one eyebrow session and one lip session, and unfortunately, I see no results that justify it.

My only advice please don’t rely solely on what is promised during consultation. Ask detailed questions, understand the number of sittings required, and proceed only when everything is clearly documented.
